text:
Ivar Stenberg went second overall to the Sharks in June, one pick after Gavin McKenna, and at 19 he is already a regular on a young Sharks team. Seventeen points in 28 games, nine of them on the power play, and his minutes have climbed almost three a night over the last ten games, to about 18 and a half. NHL.com's rookie watch has him trending up.

He is ahead of the usual curve. Forwards picked in the top four since 2005 averaged 0.56 points a game in their first full season; Stenberg is at 0.61. His own chances run at 1.01 expected goals per 60 minutes, eight goals on 8.0 expected, which means the finishing is exactly what it should be.

The bad luck is around him. San Jose has scored 9.2 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice and that has cost him points. Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest noted he has started seeing shifts with Macklin Celebrini and Will Smith. That is the spot to watch.
